text:
jamal: seeing 401 invalid_api_key from our staging service after a key rotation. only happens for the containerized worker, local dev with the same key works fine.

jamal: curl output: 
```
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid or expired"}
```

jamal: our Dockerfile has these lines (simplified):
```
ARG API_KEY
ENV API_KEY=$API_KEY
COPY . /app
CMD ["/app/entrypoint.sh"]
```

jamal: inside the running container `env | grep API_KEY` prints `API_KEY=${API_KEY}` (literally). so looks like the value never got substituted.

liz: that explains the 401 — sending the literal token placeholder is treated as an invalid key. did you build with `--build-arg API_KEY=...` or are you expecting runtime env injection? ARG is build-time only.

jamal: we thought ARG would pick up the value from the host at runtime. our CI builds the image without `--build-arg`, then kubernetes sets env in the deployment yaml via `value: ${API_KEY}` from a k8s secret injection.

ashok: yep two problems at once: 1) ARG only works during build; if you don't pass build-arg you'll get empty/placeholder expansion at build-time. 2) `${API_KEY}` in YAML won't be expanded by k8s — that's a shell/local substitution pattern. If the resulting image had `ENV API_KEY=${API_KEY}` baked in literally, the container will use that literal string unless you override at runtime via env.

ashok: quick repro steps you can run locally:
```
docker build -t badimage .          # build without --build-arg
docker run --rm badimage env | grep API_KEY
# you'll see API_KEY=${API_KEY}
```

ops-bot: check: account id 987654, last 4 digits of key provided? please don't paste the full key in public channels.

jamal: account 987654, i can DM the last 4.

liz: probable fixes (pick one):
- pass secret at runtime (k8s secret -> env var) and remove ARG/ENV bake-in. e.g. in k8s deployment spec:
```
env:
  - name: API_KEY
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: redwood-api-key
        key: api_key
```
- OR if you must bake, build with `--build-arg API_KEY=$(cat /path/to/secret)` in your CI and ensure no literal placeholder remains.
- verify header quickly from the pod: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- env | grep API_KEY` and `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- curl -s -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/whoami`

jamal: thanks — we switched to mounting k8s secret as env var and removed ARG/ENV lines, redeployed. requests now return 200.

jamal: learned: don't rely on Dockerfile ARG for runtime secrets. also made CI fail the build if `--build-arg` not provided so we don't accidentally bake placeholders. :white_check_mark:

ashok: if you rotated keys in Redwood, make sure the new secret was put into the k8s secret name referenced by the deployment; if you need us to check logs or the specific failing request we can look up the rejection event (DM the last 4).

jamal: DMed the last 4, thanks for quick help — marking resolved but keeping an eye on canaries. :+1:
